title: Prohibiting Cell Death in Human Corneal Stromal Cells: New Insights for Non-surgical Keratoconus
text:
Stromal cell apoptosis plays essential roles in keratoconus pathology, which can be inhibited through covalent
and non-covalent ligands. This project established an advanced drug screening pipeline facilitated by high-
throughput technologies including mass spectrometry, in-cell ELISA, and glycan microarrays. The proposed
analytical platform has great potential to discover novel non-surgical keratoconus therapies targeting the
extrinsic apoptosis pathway and can be also utilized in other corneal dystrophies.

title: Assessing the spatial and temporal scales of attention effects and attention-dependent cholinergic release in macque V4.
text:
Attention importantly constrains vision, filtering sensory information so the brain only receives what it needs to
act. But its mechanisms have been enigmatic since its formalization by William James (1890). My project will be
the first to rigorously test the validity of the pervading hypothesis that release of the neuromodulator acetylcholine
supports attention. Results from this will deepen our understanding of the core principles governing vision,
cortical information encoding and representation, and neurological diseases in which attention is disrupted (e.g.,
schizophrenia, dementia), where interventions affecting cholinergic signaling have had variable results.

title: Computational methods for delineating cell context-specific regulatory programs
text:
Transcriptional programs control the development and functionality of specialized cell types and states. We
propose to develop transformative computational frameworks by integrating single-cell multi-omics datasets for
systematically determining transcription factors driving cellular identity to study a diverse set of developmental
and disease processes.

title: Cilia calcium dysregulation in polycystic kidney disease
text:
Mutations in PKD2 cause many forms of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). PKD2 forms
an ion channel in primary cilia of the collecting duct and aberrant cilia Ca2+ is proposed to initiate cyst formation.
We propose Ca2+ regulates PKD2 function though sites commonly mutated in the ADPKD population. We have
developed novel tools to study the structural and functional biophysics of cilia PKD2— which yield results in
real-time, at super and atomic resolution– thereby providing the most accurate description of the disease-
causing mechanism involved in cilia Ca2+-dependent gene expression changes during cyst formation.

title: Enhancing cone survival in retinitis pigmentosa through cell-specific therapeutic CRISPR editing of a roxadustat target
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it is expected to increase understanding of the
pathogenesis of retinitis pigmentosa, the most common inherited retinal dystrophy, while testing a potential
metabolic reprogramming therapy in a mouse model. Thus, the proposed research is relevant to the part of the
NEI’s mission that pertains to supporting vision research to protect and prolong vision.

title: Identifying unrecognized genetic causes of congenital heart disease
text:
Congenital heart disease (CHD), the most common human birth defect, occurs in ~1% of live births and has a
genetic cause in almost 45% cases. Genetic variants of unknown significance may contribute to unexplained
CHD. We will study these variants to determine their functional impact on cardiac cells.

title: Distinct roles of neural crest cell populations in cranial suture development and disease
text:
Craniosynostosis, the fusion of skull and facial bones, is among the most common of childbirth defects (148,000
cases per year) that limits the lifespan, physical growth, and cognitive development of children. Patients suffer
several corrective post-operative refusion surgeries. While the conserved signals that maintain separate skull
bones remain unknown, my findings will reveal the cellular basis of premature skull fusions in Bent Bone
Dysplasia, Apert and Pfeiffer syndromes, three human disorders that cause devastating skull deformities and
neonatal death.

title: RUNX proteins define opposing fates in the male germline
text:
Ongoing studies demonstrate that male infertility can originate from disruptions during prepubertal development
as the germline prepares for continuous sperm production. However, because the factors that regulate
prepubertal germline development are largely unknown, progress towards diagnosing, preventing, or even
treating male infertility has been stifled. The proposed studies will generate fundamental insights into the
mechanisms that govern germ cell development, including that of the germline stem cell population and fate
decisions that ultimately lay the groundwork for sperm production throughout reproductive years.

title: Cellular Mechanisms of Neuroligin-4 Gene in Human Neurons
text: The cellular function of Neuroligin-4 (NLGN4), a human-specific synaptic protein, remains unclear due to its poor expression and minimal sequence conservation in conventional rodent models. We will derive human neuronal subtypes from pluripotent stem cells to determine NLGN4’s role at synapses, and examine how different domains and residues regulate NLGN4’s mechanistic properties. Our approach will provide novel insights into NLGN4-dependent unique synaptic processes that operate specifically in a human brain.

title: Training Program in Brain Tumor Biology
text:
The multidisciplinary University of Alabama at Birmingham Training Program in Brain Tumor Biology is focused
on preparing highly motivated pre-doctoral and MD/PhD students for a career in fundamental and translational
brain tumor research. Trainees are therefore selected for their commitment to neuro-oncology research and excellent
performance in the first two years of the UAB Graduate Biomedical Sciences Program. Our dedicated and
collaborative training environment provides the ideal setting for implementation of an educational
program in brain tumor research.

title: Mitochondrial Gene Editing in Human Cardiomyocytes
text:
Mitochondria (mt) are regarded as critical components for heart muscle cells and crucial for normal cardiac
function. This project uses new gene editing technology to study mitochondria in human heart muscle cells.

title: Molecular and Fitness Barriers to Bunyavirus Reassortment
text:
The ability of viruses to rapidly evolve allows viruses to jump into new hosts, escape immunity,
and generally cause problems. This project will generate an improved understanding of the
details of how viruses evolve. This will allow scientists to better predict the risk posed by certain
viruses and reveal new ways to combat dangerous viruses.

title: The interaction effects of genetic variants, age, diet, sex and mitochondrial copy number on Alzheimer's disease, aging-phenotypes and longevity
text:
In this project, we will quantify the relationship between genetic variants, age, diet, sex, mitochondrial DNA
copy number, longevity and Alzheimer’s disease using a diverse cohort of BXD and transgenic AD-BXD
mouse lines, which segregate for over 6 million genetic variants. This approach allows a chain of causality
between genetic variants, environmental effects, cellular processes, and whole-organism outcomes, such as
cognitive decline in aging. The use of a genetically and environmentally reproducible population will allow us
to integrate all of our data with a previously collected phenome of over 7500 traits and over 110 omics
datasets, including longevity, memory, learning, motor, and neuroanatomical phenotypes, as well as translate
across species using human genome-wide (GWAS) and phenome-wide (PheWAS) association study data.

title: Development of a Rabbit Model for Myeloperoxidase Deficiency
text:
Myeloperoxidase (MPO), which gives the distinctive green tinge in pus and phlegm, is the key enzyme that
generates chlorine bleach in white blood cells for bacterial killing, and patients lacking this enzyme often
contract fungal infection and develop inflammatory diseases. Because the existing MPO-deficient mouse
model fails to reproduce the human disease, an accurate and faithful animal model is critically needed. The
current application has laid out a comprehensive plan to characterize a novel MPO-deficient rabbit model to
meet the need for basic research of MPO-related infection and inflammatory diseases.

title: Administrative Core for Institution # 269291
text: The main objective of the Central Administrative and Management Core (CAMC) is to serve as the anchor and to provide administrative oversight for the Comprehensive NeuroHIV Center (CNHC) at Temple University and Drexel University in Philadelphia. The overall objective is to improve and expand research related to neuroHIV and neurological diseases associated with viral infection of the CNS including neurobehavioral impairment and mental disorders. The infrastructure created by the CNHC during the last 10 years offers unique expertise to local, regional, and national neuroHIV investigators with focus on our strengths of gene editing and delivery, mammalian progenitor cells and iPSC cultures, assist investigators with genetic analysis of virus-infected cells before and after editing procedures, and support for a full-range of state-of-the-art microscopic and imaging analysis. At the same time, the CNHC will coordinate the NeuroHIV Community Partnership Core, the newly developed core that is now included in our program, to assist with liaising with current and potential community partners in fostering synergy among the patient population and the participant researchers. The Center offers its unique expertise in functional cellular assays including microelectrode array assay to study neuronal cell behavior in response to external stress. Furthermore, the Center will enable investigators to initiate clinical and neurobehavioral examination with a well-established cohort of people with HIV (PWH) longitudinally examined at Drexel University College of Medicine. The CAMC will provide the infrastructure for coordinating and overseeing all activities of the CNHC and facilitating synergistic interaction among the cores and other NIMH-supported Centers. The CAMC will delineate the strategic plan, identify short- and long-term objectives, execute detailed plans to be implemented, carry out internal and external reviews and assessment tools based on established criteria to ensure productive and efficient use of resources to achieve the overall objectives of the CNHC. It will also offer biostatistical support for data analysis and interpretation obtained from the basic science and clinical cores. In addition, this Core will coordinate with the Scientific Cores to disseminate information to the participants as well as Core users, recruit Core users, solicit pilot applications, catalogue all original data generated by the Cores, facilitate and track all material distributed by the Cores, including, but not limited to, cell lines, viral stocks, and clinical specimens.

title: Tailoring Stress Cardiac MRI for Women with Ischemic Heart Disease
text:
TO PUBLIC HEALTH
Ischemic heart disease due to non-obstructive coronary stenosis and small vessel dysfunction (coronary
microvascular disease, CMD) is more common than previously thought. The underdiagnosis of CMD and lack
of therapeutic options have resulted from our myopic view of obstructive coronary stenosis as the only reason
for chest pain and the requirement for invasive coronary testing. We aim to improve the management of CMD
by further targeting our high-resolution cardiac MRI framework and developing methods for non-invasive
estimation of patient-specific coronary hemodynamic parameters; both will enable detection, monitoring, and
testing of therapeutic interventions for CMD.

title: Engineering Salmonella-based Platforms for Immunotherapy Against Immunologically Silent Tumors
text:
Cancer remains one of the most formidable challenges in medicine. Solid “cold” tumors, in particular, pose
significant therapeutic hurdles due to poor vascularization, hypoxia, and an immunosuppressive 
microenvironment that diminishes the effectiveness of existing treatments. By integrating S. Typhimurium's
tumor-targeting and immunostimulatory capabilities with novel strategies to bolster anti-tumor immune 
responses, this research proposes an innovative approach to overcoming these obstacles.

title: Advanced Gene Mapping Course
text: There is a great need for training in the analysis of genetic data. Although vast amounts of omics data are generated, the number of researchers with the ability to perform data analysis is insufficient. The Advanced Gene Mapping Course provides researchers with the knowledge and skills to analyze these data to make important discoveries in the genetics of complex traits which in turn will lead to improved disease diagnosis and treatment modalities.

title: Molecular and cellular characterization of essential human genes.
text:
In this proposal, which is written in response to the MorPhic consortium, our center
will create a barcoded, chemically inducible, and reversible system to deplete protein of interest. To achieve this, we utilize a sensitive auxin-inducible degron (AID) to degrade the target proteins with a
small chemical molecule rapidly. We will create this unique null allele generation resource for 250
critical genes in human induced pluripotent cell. The obtained information will demonstrate the
feasibility of this strategy for the ultimate goal of the MorPhic. It will reveal the biological roles of a large
number of developmentally critical genes that are not amenable to chronic deletion.

title: ROAR Career Enhancement Core
text: ABSTRACT – CAREER ENHANCEMENT CORE With early recognition through expanded newborn screening and advances in management leading to improved outcomes and survival, the number of children and adults with inborn errors of metabolism, particularly organic acidemias, continues to grow. Despite the increased need, the number of physicians and other medical providers with clinical and research expertise in inborn errors of metabolism is limited. According to statistics from the American Board of Medical Genetics and Genomics, 10 U.S. states have no physicians with advanced training in inborn errors of metabolism (i.e. certification in either medical or clinical biochemical genetics). This lack of physician providers with expertise in metabolic disorders impacts the delivery of acute and chronic care for patients with these diagnoses. Likewise, this lack of physician-researchers with a focus on metabolic disease impacts the design and implementation of clinical trials for these rare disorders and limits the participation of some individuals with inborn errors of metabolism in these trials due to lack of access to them. Moreover, a recent constituent survey conducted by the Organic Acidemias Association and Propionic Acidemia Foundation identified “access to care” as the top concern across all disorders. To address these significant gaps, the Rare Organic Acidemias Research (ROAR) consortium Career Enhancement Core (CEC) will develop a comprehensive strategy for recruiting and retaining a cohort of physicians and physician-researchers with clinical and research expertise in rare metabolic disorders, specifically organic acidemias. The strategy of the ROAR CEC will integrate early exposure to the field of inborn errors of metabolism for predoctoral trainees with more advanced research training and career development activities that facilitate the recruitment and retention of postdoctoral trainees and junior faculty in the field of inborn errors of metabolism. Both predoctoral and postdoctoral trainees will be fully integrated into the consortium and receive one-on-one mentoring, participate in monthly consortium meetings, attend the annual consortium in-person meeting, attend patient advocacy group meetings, and present their research in these settings as well as at the RDCRN steering committee meetings. Moreover, the training will be personally tailored to each trainee’s academic level and career goals. The ROAR CEC will achieve these training goals with the following specific aims: 1) Introduce predoctoral level trainees to careers in rare disease clinical research and clinical care with a particular focus on inborn errors of metabolism. 2) Train postdoctoral level trainees for careers in rare disease clinical research and clinical care with a focus on inborn errors of metabolism and 3) Implement a strategy to recruit a cohort of trainees from institutions that do not have medical genetics or inborn errors of metabolism expertise to improve access to care.
